key_insight: D-Gun-sprayed NiCrAlY delivered higher hardness and corrosion resistance on Al 6061-T6, while 80Ni20Cr achieved the lowest erosion mass loss.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection should reflect the dominant damage mechanism: NiCrAlY for hardness and corrosion protection, or 80Ni20Cr for erosion resistance under the tested conditions.
method: Deposit 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 using detonation-gun thermal spraying.
Characterise microstructure, phases, roughness and hardness using SEM-EDS, XRD, AFM and nanoindentation.
Evaluate corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, wettability and solid-particle erosion.
evidence_signal: NiCrAlY reached 7895.36 MPa hardness versus 780.11 MPa for 80Ni20Cr, with corrosion rates of 0.00567 and 0.01427 mm/year, respectively, versus 0.5185 mm/year for bare aluminium.
watch_item: Room-temperature corrosion tests and one erosion condition (90° impact, 40 m/s, 5 min) do not establish long-term service performance.
paper_title: Microstructure and Surface Performance of Detonation Gun Sprayed 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY Coatings on Al 6061-T6 Substrate for Structural Applications
